messages:
aleks: Heads up — seeing a weird pack/evict loop in eu-west1-c. GPUs are 'Ready' but pods get stuck Terminating and the scheduler keeps scattering tiny pods into other racks. Fragmentation + costs spike.

mira: ugh. any node-level symptoms?

aleks: Node shows Ready and allocatable GPUs, but kubelet logs show flapping: 
```
E0901 12:03:22.345 kubelet_node_status.go:123] failed to update node status: Post \"https://apiserver/api/v1/nodes/node-324/status\": dial tcp: i/o timeout
```
 networking appears intermittent to apiserver.

samir: is this only GPU nodes or a broader network problem?

aleks: looks concentrated to the gpu pool in rack-r26 (az eu-west1-c). Non-gpu nodes unaffected.

kai: Could be host firewall / iptables conntrack exhaustion from our telemetry burst? saw conntrack counts high earlier in metrics.

mira: can you paste output of `kubectl get pods -o wide` for the affected daemonset?

aleks: sure — snippet: 
```
NAME                             READY   STATUS        NODE         IP           AGE
gpu-worker-xyz-7k9m              0/1     Terminating   node-324     10.3.5.8     2h
gpu-worker-xyz-9p1f              1/1     Running       node-312     10.3.2.4     10m
```

notice the Terminating ones never finish. `kubectl describe pod` shows KillPod timed out trying to contact kubelet.

jess: opsbot reported a failed rolling restart earlier in the same AZ: `deploy-bot: rollout failed - timeout contacting kubelet on 3/12 nodes`

opsbot: @channel detected network path anomaly: 3 nodes in eu-west1-c returned tcp RST to apiserver health check (09:58–12:08).

samir: if kubelet can't reach apiserver (or vice versa) the API can't observe Pod status transitions, so Terminating stays stuck and scheduler still thinks resources are held (or miscalculates). That can cause binpacking oddness.

kai: can you check `sudo ss -s` and `sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count` on node-324? suspect conntrack max.

aleks: ran it: `nf_conntrack_count=198000, nf_conntrack_max=196608` — oh blaze. conntrack overflow around 197k, kernel started dropping.

mira: that explains weird TCP resets. Is this caused by recent telemetry rollout that opened a lot of outbound flows?

jess: yes — we shipped telemetry v2 yesterday that multiplexes traces over many short connections.

samir: immediate mitigation: bump nf_conntrack_max and restart kube-proxy? careful with memory.
kai: also can flip conntrack hashing to reduce pressure, but short term we should drain the affected nodes and force-delete stuck pods.

aleks: plan executed: `kubectl drain node-324 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force` — drain hangs because pods stuck Terminating. we had to `kubectl delete pod --grace-period=0 --force` for 12 pods. after that node rejoined healthy and apiserver connectivity returned.

mira: can you confirm scheduler metrics? did fragmentation drop after manual deletes?

aleks: fragments went from 78% to 43% after evacuating 4 bad nodes. but cost for the day shot up because we spawned new single-gpu jobs across racks.

samir: root cause: conntrack exhaustion on gpu rack nodes due to telemetry rollout creating many short-lived sockets. Effects: kubelet->apiserver timeouts, pods stuck Terminating, scheduler misreads allocations leading to small-pod scattering and GPU fragmentation.

kai: long-term fixes: 
- increase conntrack max on GPU node images (with tuning by instance class)
- update telemetry to use connection pooling / gRPC keepalives
- add node-level e2e network health probe that sets `NetworkUnavailable` sooner so scheduler can avoid placing pods during partial network outages
- make scheduler consider node NetworkUnavailable / kubelet connectivity as a hard predicate for GPU scheduling

jess: +1 on connection pooling, also think we should add an automated drain when node kubelet heartbeat drops < 60s but node still Ready. currently Ready keeps it in scheduling set.

opsbot: action created: INFRA-3245 "conntrack tuning + node network readiness predicate" assigned @kai and @mira, priority P1.

mira: I'll make a hotfix for the node image to bump nf_conntrack_max to 300k for the GPU ami and roll as a canary to eu-west1-c.

aleks: Also putting a temporary autoscale policy cap to avoid aggressive tiny job scheduling that amplifies fragmentation while we remediate.

samir: small ops note: when you force-delete Terminating pods we lose clean Gpu driver unload sometimes — watch for stuck driver modules on node restart. add a short delay to allow graceful driver cleanup in the drain runbook.

kai: agreed. will add steps: check `nvidia-smi` and `lsof /dev/nvidia*` after force deletes.

jess: cost impact estimate? how many GPU hours wasted?

aleks: rough: 18 preempted single-GPU jobs across racks x ~2h each = ~36 GPU hours. at committed rates that's ~$900 extra today. messy but manageable.

mira: followups: 1) emergency node image push (nf_conntrack bump) 2) telemetry pool fix 3) scheduler predicate PR 4) update drain runbook. I'll own 1 and 4.

samir: I'll pair with @kai on the scheduler predicate change, let's add test harness to simulate partial apiserver blackhole.

aleks: thanks all — rolling remediation now, please post any flaps. :thumbsup:
